comments.content: Stale `attachPaths` can leak across rapid workflow switches — `setAttachPaths(detail.attachments ?? [])` is called immediately after the `await` but **before** the `seq !== openSeqRef.current` guard on the next line. Every other field (activeId, name, goal, nodes, etc.) is correctly assigned after the seq check. If a user opens workflow A then quickly switches to B, A's attachment chips will briefly render on B's empty hero before being overwritten. Move `setAttachPaths(detail.attachments ?? [])` below the seq guard (e.g. right before `setMode("edit")`) to match the established race-guard convention used by every other state setter in this function.

Cross-platform basename mismatch — the chip displays `p.split("/").pop()` and the `aria-label` does the same. The Tauri dialog plugin returns OS-native paths, so on Windows this will render the full absolute path (e.g. `C:\Users\foo\doc.pdf`) instead of just the filename, hurting chip readability and producing awkward screen-reader announcements. Use a separator-agnostic basename (split on `/` or `\`, take the last segment, or use `path`/`@tauri-apps/api/path` which already normalizes). Consider extracting a small helper since the same pattern is duplicated twice in this block.
comments.existing_code: {p.split("/").pop()}

comments.content: Frontend doesn't reflect backend attachment limits — `workflow_decompose` caps at 12k chars/file and 48k chars total (see `PER_FILE_CAP` / `TOTAL_CAP` in `src-tauri/src/workflow_decompose.rs`). Users can currently pile on unlimited chips via repeated `addAttachments` calls, and the backend will silently truncate or drop files, producing surprising "missing context" results from the AI. Either surface a soft cap (e.g. disable "添加附件" after N chips, or show a `{count}/N` counter in the chip area) or at minimum add a `title` hint reflecting the limits. Pure UX issue — the backend is the source of truth, but the UI gives no signal.

comments.content: [critical] New-card subtasks are silently dropped. `workflow_save_locked` builds `Task { subtasks: None, .. }` here even though `node.subtasks: Option<Vec<String>>` was just parsed, validated (well, sort-of — see the comment at line 847), and threaded through. The companion export path (`workflow_file_from`, ~line 757) reads `t.subtasks.as_ref().map(|list| list.iter().map(|st| st.text.clone()).collect())`, which proves the contract is `Vec<String>` draft → `Vec<Subtask>` DB row → `Vec<String>` file. Nothing performs the `Vec<String>` → `Vec<Subtask>` conversion. Build `Subtask { id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string(), text: trimmed.to_string(), done: false }` for each entry here, applying the trim + empty-drop the inline comment at line 847 advertises. Add a round-trip test that supplies subtasks via `WorkflowNodeDraft` and asserts `tasks[0].subtasks` carries the texts.

comments.content: [medium] Silent data loss on JSON serialization failure. `serde_json::to_string(a).unwrap_or_default()` collapses any error into `""`, which is stored as a non-null empty string. The matching read path (`workflow_from_row`, line 146) parses `""` via `serde_json::from_str(...).ok()`, yielding `Ok(None)`, so a serialization hiccup silently wipes the user's attachment list on the next upsert with no audit/log. Propagate the error so the save fails loud rather than truncating to `Some(vec![])` on the next load.

comments.content: [medium] `ensure_workflows_attachments` swallows prepare/query errors via `.unwrap_or(false)`. Any failure from `conn.prepare(...)` or `stmt.query_map(...)` is collapsed to "column missing"; the subsequent `ALTER TABLE` then surfaces an unrelated "duplicate column name" or "no such table" error, hiding the real diagnostic (corrupted connection, locked DB, schema drift). Also non-atomic check-then-act: would race if `open_db` were invoked from multiple threads on first launch. Match on the concrete error and let unrelated errors propagate.

[medium] `attachments` and `subtasks` accept arbitrary strings with no cap, path validation, or per-item length check. `bot_py::doc_extract` is the only safety net for paths, and `node.subtasks` is not validated at all at this layer (the cap in `workflow_decompose::validate_decompose` is bypassed by direct `workflow_save` calls). Cap `attachments.len()` (e.g. 10), drop empty/whitespace entries, reject paths containing `..` or absolute-prefix anomalies, and apply the same trim+length+count policy to `node.subtasks` here so the file-parser comment at line 847 actually holds.

[low] Silent JSON deserialization failure on the read path hides corruption. `serde_json::from_str(&s).ok()` maps malformed JSON (partial write, manual edit, upgrade bug) to `None` with no log. Combined with the silent serialization failure in `upsert_workflow`, persistent corruption is invisible. For consistency with the analogous `task_from_row` (which `eprintln!`s a warning on `subtasks`/`files`/`budget` JSON failure), emit at least a stderr warning here.

`dirty` snapshot doesn't include `attachPaths` — adding/removing attachments never marks the workflow as dirty, so the toolbar's Save button (disabled when `!dirty`, line 781) stays disabled and users cannot persist attachment changes via the UI even though `save()` (line 570) correctly forwards `attachPaths` to the backend. Both `snapshot` (line 159-162) and the three `setSavedSnapshot` call sites (lines 182-184, 601-603) need to include the current `attachPaths` in the JSON payload. Otherwise `openWorkflow` → add attachment → Save stays greyed out → backend never receives the new paths.

EmptyHero description still mentions the removed "创建空白画布" entry point: the non-regenerate branch text (line 893) advertises a manual blank-canvas path that no longer exists in this component (per W8-ATTACH spec — `onCreateBlank` was removed from EmptyHero's props). Users reading the description will look for the button and won't find one; the only remaining route to a blank canvas is the toolbar 「新建」 button, which isn't called out here.

comments.content: Windows path separator not handled: `path.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(path)` only splits on POSIX `/`. On Windows the LLM prompt would see the full path as the filename (e.g. `C:\Users\foo\report.docx`), confusing the LLM's content routing and degrading prompt quality. The frontend already has a cross-platform `basename` helper in `src/format.ts` that splits on `/[\\/]/`. On the Rust side, prefer `std::path::Path::new(path).file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()).unwrap_or(path)` for an idiomatic cross-platform basename.
comments.existing_code: let file_name = path.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(path);

comments.content: Cap bookkeeping bug: after truncating `text` to fit `TOTAL_CAP`, `total_used` is not updated — it remains at `previous_total_used + text.chars().count()` (the pre-truncation size). With the current values (`PER_FILE_CAP=12000`, `TOTAL_CAP=48000`) the upfront `total_used >= TOTAL_CAP` guard at the start of each iteration masks the bug for file inclusion (the next iteration is correctly skipped), but the inflated `total_used` is a latent defect: if `PER_FILE_CAP` or `TOTAL_CAP` are tweaked (e.g. `PER_FILE_CAP` raised or `TOTAL_CAP` lowered), files that should fit would be wrongly skipped. Fix by assigning `total_used = TOTAL_CAP` (or `previous_total_used + remain`) after truncation.

Missing test coverage for new subtasks validation: the new logic (≤8 entries, ≤60 chars per entry, trim, empty-strip → None) has no dedicated test. The diff only added `subtasks: None` to existing test struct literals to satisfy the new field. Add at least one positive case (≤8 entries × ≤60 chars accepted with trim) and one negative case (>8 entries rejected; >60 chars rejected; all-empty list → None) to prevent regression.

Contract/code mismatch: the contract segment says "subtasks：可选，2~8 条子任务文本" but the validator only enforces the upper bound (≤8). After empty-strip, a list with 1 entry passes validation, contradicting the "2~8" contract. Either tighten the contract text to "1~8" (or "≤8") to match the lenient validator, or tighten the validator to reject single-entry lists so the contract and code agree.

comments.content: The comment at line 847 ("空串/空白子任务在保存链构建 Subtask 时再过滤") promises a `Subtask` construction step that is nowhere defined. Even when confirmed finding #1 (silent drop in workflow_save_locked) is fixed, the fix must include the actual transformation `Vec<String> → Vec<Subtask>` — each entry needs a uuid `id`, the trimmed `text`, and `done: false`. Right now no code path builds a `Subtask { id, text, done }` from `node.subtasks: Option<Vec<String>>`. The export side at workflow_file_from (line 757) extracts `Subtask::text` correctly, but the reverse mapping is missing — when bug #1 is fixed, this transformation (uuid allocation, defaults, trim, empty-strip) must land alongside it.

comments.content: `validate_nodes` does not enforce the same ≤8 subtasks × ≤60 chars limit + whitespace trim/empty-strip rules that `validate_decompose` (workflow_decompose.rs:165-187) applies to LLM output. The decompose-path validation is unreachable from `workflow_save` (which only calls `validate_nodes`), so a frontend-submitted `node.subtasks` with 1000 entries or 10k-char strings will silently bypass the contract that limits the AI output. Confirmed finding #4 notes "node.subtasks is not validated at all at this layer" but does not specify that the validator exists in a sibling module and is unreachable from this path — moving the validator or sharing it via `pub(crate)` would close this gap.

The tests in this module uniformly set `attachments: None` on every `WorkflowSaveInput` and `subtasks: None` on every `WorkflowNodeDraft`, exercising neither the new persistence path nor the new-card `Subtask` construction. Round-trip coverage is missing for: (a) saving a workflow with `attachments: Some(vec!["/tmp/x.pdf"])` and reading it back via `load_workflow`; (b) submitting `node.subtasks: Some(vec!["子任务 1", "子任务 2"])` through `workflow_save_locked` and reading the resulting `Task.subtasks` back as `Vec<Subtask>`. These tests would have caught confirmed findings #1 (silent drop) and #2/#5 (silent JSON ser/de) at the unit level — a single test per gap is sufficient.

comments.content: `attached_ok` overcounts when extraction returns empty content: an `Ok(res)` whose `res.text` is empty (or whose `PER_FILE_CAP` slice is empty) still increments `attached_ok`, so the audit and the prompt header claim "X 个读取成功" for files that produced no usable text. The prompt then carries a `【附件 N：filename】` block with an empty body, wasting tokens and confusing the LLM. Only count `attached_ok += 1` when `!text.is_empty()` (or fold empty successes into the total-cap / failure branch).

Subtask 60-char error message does not identify which entry failed: with up to 8 subtasks per task the user (and the LLM retried after `fail!`) sees "第 2 个任务的子任务超过 60 字上限" but has no idea which of the up to 8 entries is the offender. The `value` field holds the offending text but `reason` should also include the entry index and a short preview (e.g. `第 2 个任务的第 5 条子任务超过 60 字上限（前缀："..."`)) so the error is actionable when surfaced to the user.

No upper bound on number of attachments: the loop iterates the full `attachment_list` and calls `doc_extract` per entry (each may be a multi-second subprocess + Python docx/xlsx/pptx/pdf load). With `PER_FILE_CAP=12_000` and `TOTAL_CAP=48_000` a malicious or buggy caller passing thousands of paths would burn wall-clock time and per-attachment audit overhead before the character cap ever stops the loop. Add a hard count cap (e.g. 8–16) at the top of the loop with the same skip-with-placeholder pattern as the character-cap branch.

`value` field for the >8 entries error holds `list.len().to_string()` — the count, not the offending content — inconsistent with the title/note validators that put the actual offending string in `value`. For machine-readable error location, dump the joined list (truncated) or at minimum the count plus first entry; otherwise grep-style consumers can't pinpoint which list blew past the cap.
